explanations: terra: God seals the disbelievers' hearts and hearing and places a covering on sight; rejection becomes an identifying divine impression upon the faculties that sustained it.

luna: The section's proposed sense of ٱسْم as a distinguishing mark meets the naming of every thing to Adam; names separate and identify what is otherwise undifferentiated. | terra: God teaches Adam the names and asks that the named things be identified, giving اسم the practical work of distinguishing one thing from another.
luna: Those who buy worldly life in exchange for the Hereafter face unlightened punishment; this is another direct statement of a choice that marks the person for an outcome.
terra: The calf is made to sink into their hearts through disbelief; the chosen object of worship leaves an inward attachment by which the people are known.

luna: صبغة الله, God's dye, gives the believers a marked identity; it is a specific metaphor for belonging, though not the section's proposed root for ٱسْم. | terra: صِبْغَةَ ٱللَّهِ presents God's dye or coloring as an identity of worship and belonging, a close nonlexical counterpart to the Lord's mark borne by His own.
terra: The ark contains a remnant left by the houses of Moses and Aaron and is itself a sign of rightful kingship; surviving objects identify a divinely appointed owner and relation.

luna: Restrained poor people are recognized by their marks even though they do not beg; this is a compassionate, positive counterpart to a punitive brand. | terra: تَعْرِفُهُم بِسِيمَاهُمْ directs the giver to recognize the restrained poor by their sign despite their refusal to ask, so an unspoken condition is read from a trace.

luna: The list of worldly attractions includes wealth, livestock, and fields, all described as enjoyment of near life while the good return is with Allah; it gives concrete objects one may prefer over what remains. | terra: ٱلْخَيْلِ ٱلْمُسَوَّمَةِ places marked or branded horses inside the adornments of worldly life, then calls all of them temporary enjoyment; it joins the section's animal brand directly to its reading of preferring الدنيا.

terra: Immediately after the marked horses and worldly adornments of 3:14, the hearer is asked whether he wants news of something better; the contrast supplies the right valuation of the branded-animal scene.

luna: Faces become white or black on the Day of Judgment, publicly separating groups; the face carries a moral sign, unlike the single mark of prostration. | terra: Some faces whiten and others blacken on the Day, making opposed allegiances legible on their bearers before punishment is pronounced.
terra: Those whose faces whiten enter God's mercy permanently, supplying the good visible sign opposite the darkened face of 3:106.
terra: The promised angels are مُسَوِّمِينَ, marked or marking according to the reading; the disputed sense still extends the w-s-m identity-sign from livestock to a divinely distinguished host.
luna: At Uhud, some wanted the world and some the Hereafter; the split in preference had a consequence in the battle, giving the choice a concrete mark.
terra: Whenever the condemned person's skins are burned, they are exchanged for other skins to taste punishment; the branded hide expands into a whole skin made to bear fire's consequence.
luna: Believers are urged to sell the present life for the Hereafter; this reverses the section's preference and makes allegiance visible in a choice.

luna: The section's brand lexicon says an animal can be recognized by an ear cut or a burn; this ayah names cutting livestock ears as a satanic practice, a reversal of an identifying mark. | terra: Satan's command that people slit the ears of livestock stages the section's exact alternative to cautery for marking an animal, while exposing a mark that falsely alters God's creation.
terra: The sacrificial animals and their garlands must not be violated; the garland is a visible, non-burning livestock sign that marks the animal as consecrated to God.

luna: The trained hunting animal catches prey, and Allah's name is mentioned over the catch; this is another specific case where the name marks an animal as lawfully dedicated to its Lord. | terra: Hunters are told to mention God's name over what trained animals catch, using the name to identify the lawful relation among owner, animal, and food.
terra: Jesus is sent عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم after the prophets, turning أثر into faithful succession: a prior bearer leaves a line that another follows.

luna: The verse denies that God instituted the named classes of marked livestock; it sets a boundary against invented ownership signs and animal categories. | terra: God denies instituting the named livestock classes baḥīrah, sāʾibah, waṣīlah, and ḥām; it rejects humanly invented animal markings as claims about divine ownership.
luna: This life's play and amusement is bounded by the better home of the Hereafter for the God-fearing; it parallels the choice that reveals allegiance.
luna: Allah knows every fallen leaf and every seed hidden in the earth; the root ع ل م from the section meets its concern with visible and hidden traces in a specific scene of plant remains.
terra: After people fabricate sons and daughters for God, He is glorified above their descriptions; this is an explicit purification of the Lord's identity from defective attribution.

luna: The verse says to eat what has Allah's name mentioned over it; spoken naming marks the animal as dedicated to its true owner. | terra: Eating what God's name has been mentioned over makes the name a practical sign of lawful dedication, close to the section's ownership-mark reading of اسم.
luna: This ayah continues 6:118 by asking why people would not eat what has Allah's name mentioned over it and clarifying the exception; it spells out the boundary conveyed by naming the offering.

luna: The inverse boundary is explicit: an animal without Allah's name mentioned over it is not to be eaten, and the verse associates that omission with disobedience and satanic prompting. | terra: The prohibition on eating what God's name was not mentioned over draws a boundary between two allegiances; an animal without the true owner's name becomes a site of satanic dispute.

luna: People assign portions of crops and cattle to God and partners, then misdirect them; this exposes false claims of ownership against the section's true Lord. | terra: People allocate crops and livestock between God and their alleged partners, staging rival claims of ownership that the section's true Lord-mark is meant to distinguish.

terra: The pagans invent livestock restrictions and animals عَلَيْهَا ٱفْتِرَآءً عَلَيْهِ over which God's name is not mentioned; the absent name exposes a counterfeit claim of ownership and consecration.
terra: The invented livestock rules assign what is in animal wombs by sex and status; false ownership-signs continue by deciding who may possess or consume the marked stock.

luna: Prayer, sacrifice, life, and death are declared for Allah, Lord of the worlds; this makes the section's owner-mark concrete as a whole life identified with its Lord. | terra: Prayer, sacrifice, life, and death are declared لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ; the whole self and its animal offering are assigned to the named Lord-owner.
terra: وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ states the section's lexicographic claim almost verbatim: the sought Lord is the Lord and owner of every thing.

luna: People on the heights recognize each group by its marks; 7:48 continues their address to those recognized, a direct scene of identity read from signs. | terra: The people on the Heights يَعْرِفُونَ كُلًّۢا بِسِيمَاهُمْ, recognizing every group by its marks; the sign visibly distinguishes belonging and fate.

luna: The men of the heights call people they recognize by their marks; the dialogue completes 7:46's image of a sign distinguishing persons. | terra: The people on the Heights address men whom they know بِسِيمَاهُمْ; this continuation shows a mark identifying particular persons even before their final admission is announced.

luna: Hud challenges the people over names they and their fathers assigned without God's authority; the section's name-as-mark reading meets a boundary where naming cannot establish rightful ownership. | terra: Hūd calls the alleged deities mere names coined by the people and their fathers without authority, exposing labels that claim sacred identity but bear no true owner's warrant.

luna: Allah owns the most beautiful names and is invoked by them; the command to leave those who distort His names parallels the section's call to keep the Lord's identifying name free of flaw. | terra: God owns the beautiful names and the hearer is told to leave those who distort them; this directly supports hearing “glorify your Lord's name” as keeping His identifying name pure.
luna: Family, wealth, trade, and homes become a boundary when they are dearer than Allah and His Messenger; the verse makes worldly preference a public allegiance.

luna: Heated gold and silver are pressed against hoarders' foreheads, sides, and backs; the fire-brand is a punishment mark, reversing the section's mark of belonging to the Lord. | terra: Hoarded gold and silver are heated in Hell and used to cauterize foreheads, sides, and backs; the very worldly thing chosen becomes the fire-brand carried on the chooser's body.

luna: The challenge asks whether people are content with this life instead of the Hereafter, whose enjoyment is small; it gives the preference a clear limit. | terra: The rebuke asks whether people are content with worldly life instead of the Hereafter and calls its enjoyment slight; it names the valuation behind the section's marked preference.
luna: Those content with worldly life and heedless of God's signs are the reverse of the one who fears and remembers; this joins the section's preference and sign themes.
luna: The next ayah gives those heedless people the Fire as their abode for what they earned, completing 10:7's choice of worldly life with the section's fire-mark.
luna: The worldly life is compared to vegetation that flourishes, then becomes harvest debris; this is another direct rendering of growth passing into a trace.
terra: The doers of good receive the best, and neither darkness nor abasement covers their faces; their faces are protected from the evil mark.

luna: Evil-doers' faces are covered with patches like night and humiliation; the visible stain reverses the good trace of prostration. | terra: Evil earners have faces covered as though by pieces of dark night and are identified as companions of the Fire; deed, face-trace, and fire meet.
terra: Pharaoh's body is preserved so that he may be a sign for those after him; the dead bearer becomes a surviving, readable mark of the allegiance and judgment that claimed him.
luna: People who want worldly life and its adornment are a direct counterpart to those who prefer it in 87:16; their aim exposes what they prize.
luna: The next ayah says such people have no share in the Hereafter, their work is nullified, and they meet the Fire; it makes the passing choice's consequence explicit.
terra: The overthrow of Lot's towns and the rain of baked-clay stones supplies both the ruined scene and the objects that 11:83 calls marked at the Lord.
terra: The stones that punish Lot's people are مُسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ, marked at or by the Lord; mark, Lord, ownership, and judgment coincide in one phrase.

terra: بَقِيَّتُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكُمْ makes what God leaves or preserves “better” for the hearers, closely joining the section's definition of أثر as a بقية to its contrast between the better remainder and preferred gain.

luna: The brothers display Joseph's shirt with false blood; a fabricated trace can mislead, so the section's act of reading signs requires discernment. | terra: Joseph's brothers bring his shirt with false blood, manufacturing a misleading bodily trace; it is the boundary case showing that a visible أثر can be forged and must be read truthfully.
terra: Joseph proposes that the direction of the torn shirt be read as evidence, turning a physical remainder into a discriminator between truth and accusation.

luna: The torn shirt is used as a diagnostic mark: a tear from behind means Joseph was fleeing, so a bodily trace identifies the action and the truthful speaker. | terra: A rear tear would mark Joseph as truthful and his accuser as lying; this ayah states explicitly how one trace distinguishes moral identities.

luna: After the shirt is shown torn from behind, the husband reads that physical trace as proof of the truth; 12:27 supplies the test, making a mark distinguish whose claim is sound. | terra: When the husband sees the shirt torn from behind, he reads the trace and reaches judgment; it is the concrete act of tawassum without the root.

luna: Joseph says the supposed gods are only names people assigned, with no authority, while judgment belongs to Allah; this bounds the section's disputed reading of name as a mark of true ownership. | terra: The alleged gods are only names coined by people and their fathers without God's authority; an empty name is the opposite of the true Lord's ownership-sign.
terra: لَقَدْ ءَاثَرَكَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا makes preference God's act of distinguishing Joseph from his brothers, a different agent and moral direction from humans preferring the nearer life.

luna: Those who love worldly life over the Hereafter and obstruct God's path embody the preference whose trace identifies a person. | terra: Those who يَسْتَحِبُّونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا عَلَى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ enact the same preference without the أثر verb, and their obstruction shows the conduct that choice produces.
terra: The dawn blast that seizes Lot's people supplies the audible catastrophe whose physical aftermath the mutawassim reads in 15:75.

luna: The overturned town and rain of stones are the physical remainder behind 15:75's signs for discerners; the ruin itself supplies what the reader inspects. | terra: Turning the city upside down and raining baked-clay stones creates the ruined trace read in 15:75; this ayah contributes the destruction itself.

luna: The section's dictionary root و س م appears in الْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ, those who discern signs; the ruined place becomes readable evidence, the inverse use of a brand to identify a person. | terra: لِلْمُتَوَسِّمِينَ names those who discern signs in the overturned city; the reader of a brand becomes the reader of judgment from a ruin's surviving trace.

luna: The ruined place lies on an established road; after 15:75 calls it a sign for discerners, this ayah makes the mark something travelers continue to encounter. | terra: The ruined settlement lies بِسَبِيلٍۢ مُّقِيمٍ, on an enduring road; it explains how the discerning readers of 15:75 can encounter and read the city's remaining trace.
terra: After the ruin, the road, and the discerning readers, the passage explicitly calls the scene a sign for believers; it confirms that the physical remainder is meant to be read.

luna: The section's note on the root ع ل م links knowing to a mark that distinguishes; عَلَامَاتٍ here are landmarks that identify a route, with stars also guiding travelers. | terra: وَعَلَـٰمَـٰتٍۢ وَبِٱلنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ uses the knowledge-root for distinguishing landmarks; a readable mark makes direction knowable exactly as the section's root definition says.
terra: The face of one given news of a daughter darkens while he suppresses grief; an inward valuation becomes immediately readable on the face.

luna: What people possess will end, while what is with Allah remains; this directly develops أثر as remainder and the section's worldly/lasting contrast. | terra: مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَاقٍ draws the section's أثر-as-remainder boundary explicitly: human possessions vanish, while what belongs with God remains.
luna: The disbelievers are described as having preferred worldly life over the Hereafter; the same priority leaves a defining allegiance.
luna: Following 16:107's statement that they preferred worldly life, this ayah says their hearts, hearing, and sight are sealed; the preference leaves a spiritual mark.
terra: Every person's طَـٰٓئِرَهُ is fastened to his neck and his record is brought out, giving each person an attached, individualized sign of what he chose and did.

luna: Whoever wants the immediate life is given what God wills, then faces blame and Hell; the choice leaves a consequence, as in the section's fire-mark contrast. | terra: Whoever desires the immediate life receives a measured share and then is assigned Hell; the desired world culminates in the fire-sign attached to that choice.

luna: Whoever wants the Hereafter and strives as a believer has effort acknowledged; this is the opposite trace to the worldly preference of 87:16. | terra: Whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it has effort gratefully recognized; the alternative preference leaves an accepted rather than fiery أثر.

terra: Calling on Allah or the Merciful is directed toward the same bearer of the beautiful names, while the prayer voice is disciplined; it protects divine naming from both false division and improper utterance.
terra: The Prophet is pictured following after the rejecters' traces and nearly consuming himself in grief; the departing people leave a relational and emotional أثر even when absent.
luna: Those who call on their Lord morning and evening seek His face; the Prophet is told not to turn away toward worldly adornment, joining remembrance with a refusal of status marks.
luna: The world's life is likened to rain-fed growth that becomes dry stubble scattered by wind; the plant's remaining debris meets the section's trace-as-remainder and worldly-life contrast.

luna: Wealth and children are adornment of worldly life, while الباقيات الصالحات are better and lasting; the enduring deeds are a good trace after worldly marks fade. | terra: Worldly wealth and children are adornment, while lasting righteous deeds are better with the Lord; what one does leaves the better remainder than what one displays.

luna: The youths turn back عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِمَا, retracing their steps; the section's root ء ث ر includes an iron stamp that makes a camel's footprint recognizable on earth. | terra: Moses and his servant return عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًا, following their own tracks; this supplies the literal ground-trace by which a path and its walkers are recognized.
luna: The treasure beneath the wall is preserved for two orphans because their father was righteous; a parent's virtue leaves a concrete hidden remainder for those who come after.
terra: The question whether anyone is known as the Lord's namesake or equal makes His name uniquely distinguishing, supporting the section's demand that the owner's mark remain unmixed.
terra: ٱلْبَـٰقِيَـٰتُ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتُ are better with the Lord in reward and return, giving the section's enduring أثر an ethical content.
terra: Allah alone is God and owns the beautiful names; true naming therefore identifies the one owner rather than creating competing sacred claimants.

luna: لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ uses the section's root ء ث ر in the opposite choice: the magicians will not prefer Pharaoh over clear proofs, choosing the Lord's sign over worldly coercion. | terra: The magicians say لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَـٰتِ and refuse to prefer Pharaoh over clear signs and their Creator, reversing the choice of the nearer life.

luna: The magicians say they believe in their Lord and that Allah is better and more lasting; this completes 20:72's refusal to prefer Pharaoh and the worldly power he commands. | terra: وَٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ follows the refusal to prefer Pharaoh, matching the section's “the Hereafter is better and more lasting” and showing what correct preference leaves one loyal to.
terra: Hell is where the criminal لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحْيَىٰ, the same neither-dead-nor-alive fire consequence that follows the section's worldly preference.
terra: Coming to the Lord as a believer with righteous deeds yields the highest ranks, supplying the personal alternative to the criminal who bears the neither-dead-nor-alive fire fate in 20:74.
terra: Everlasting gardens are the purified believers' reward, completing the opposite enduring destination after the magicians refuse to prefer Pharaoh.
terra: Moses says his people are عَلَىٰٓ أَثَرِى, on his trace; the word marks a relation of following and belonging, the relational remainder in the section's أثر definition.

luna: The Samiri says he took a handful from أَثَرِ الرَّسُولِ; the same root named in the section makes a remaining trace carry the absent messenger's presence. | terra: The Samaritan takes a handful مِنْ أَثَرِ ٱلرَّسُولِ and casts it into the calf; a physical trace is misappropriated to manufacture a false object of allegiance.

luna: The Prophet is told not to fix his eyes on worldly splendor, since his Lord's provision is better and more lasting; this turns preference into a visible discipline of attention. | terra: The eye must not reach toward worldly splendor because وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ; the Lord-owner's provision is better and more lasting than the preferred display.
terra: Honoring God's شعائر is said to come from the piety of hearts; the outward belonging-sign on rites and animals is traced back to an inward mark.

luna: Each community has rites in which God's name is mentioned over the livestock He provides; the name marks whose provision and offering the animal is. | terra: Each community receives a rite so that God's name may be mentioned over the livestock He provided; name, provider-owner, and marked ritual animal form the section's scene.

luna: Camels are made among God's rites, and His name is spoken over them as they stand; this joins the camel brand scene to a mark of dedication to the true owner. | terra: Sacrificial camels are called God's شعائر and His name is pronounced over them; livestock, a belonging-sign, and the owner's name meet without the need for a burned brand.

luna: Meat and blood do not reach God, only taqwa; this limits the camel and name rite outward sign to inward devotion rather than a physical brand alone. | terra: Neither sacrificial flesh nor blood reaches God; piety does. This sets the boundary between an outward animal sign and the inward allegiance that gives the rite its true mark.
terra: Protected houses of worship are defined as places where God's name is mentioned often; their preservation keeps the owner's name visibly present in the world.
terra: Ruined towns, collapsed roofs, abandoned wells, and lofty palaces present the surviving objects of destroyed communities, concrete آثار from which their fate is read.

terra: تَعْرِفُ فِى وُجُوهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ٱلْمُنكَرَ makes rejection recognizable in faces precisely while God's verses are recited, supplying the evil face-trace in the section's dictionary image.
terra: Fire scorches their faces, making punishment itself write the condemned identity onto the same facial surface on which the section reads marks.

luna: Tongues, hands, and feet testify to what people did; bodily traces identify the actions behind a person's outward appearance. | terra: Tongues, hands, and feet testify to what people used to do; conduct leaves the person bodily identifiable even without an external brand.

luna: Houses are raised for Allah's name to be remembered and glorified morning and evening; this places the Lord's name in a visible devotional setting, like an affiliation mark. | terra: God's name is remembered in houses He allowed to be raised, so a visible place and the recurring name together identify a space as belonging to His worship.
luna: Commerce does not distract these men from God's remembrance and prayer; their priorities make the name-bearing community recognizable against the world's pull.

luna: The empty houses of former wrongdoers are called a sign for those who know; built places become residual marks by which a people are recognized. | terra: The wrongdoers' houses lie empty because of what they did, and the scene is called a sign for those who know; ruin functions as an identifying remainder.

luna: Worldly gifts are enjoyment and adornment, while what is with Allah is better and more lasting; this states the precise passing/remaining relation behind the section's gloss. | terra: Worldly gifts are temporary enjoyment and adornment, while what is with God is خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ, restating the section's valuation of what passes against what remains.

luna: All things perish except the face of the Lord; this repeats the section's contrast between what passes and the enduring Lord behind the identifying mark. | terra: Everything perishes except God's face, and judgment and return belong to Him; permanence and dominion meet in the Lord-owner after all created marks disappear.
terra: The punishment descending on Lot's town for transgression creates the material remainder that 29:35 says God left as a clear sign.

luna: After Lot's town is destroyed, a clear sign is left from it for people who reason; like 15:75, the ruined place bears a readable trace of judgment. | terra: God says He left from Lot's settlement ءَايَةًۢ بَيِّنَةً, a clear surviving sign; the destroyed place itself becomes the remainder from which judgment is read.

luna: This life is amusement, while the Hereafter is the true life; the contrast gives weight to the section's trace of what remains. | terra: Worldly life is play and distraction while the Hereafter is the true life, sharpening the section's claim that preference reveals whether one bears a passing or lasting attachment.
luna: People know only the outward surface of worldly life and are heedless of the Hereafter; this contrasts their limited knowing with Allah's knowledge of public and hidden things in the section.
terra: Earlier peoples left greater ءَاثَارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ, yet their ruins survive as evidence after the people vanish; the remainder identifies a lost power and its judgment.
terra: Corruption appears on land and sea because of what people's hands earned; collective choice leaves a visible environmental trace whose makers can be inferred from it.

luna: The command to look at ءَاثَٰرِ رَحْمَتِ ٱللَّهِ makes the revived earth a visible remainder of mercy, an effect that lets a reader recognize its source. | terra: فَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِ رَحْمَتِ ٱللَّهِ asks the reader to recognize God's mercy from its effects on dead earth, a benevolent version of knowing an owner through what His act leaves behind.
luna: When believers are reminded of God's signs, they fall in prostration and glorify Him without arrogance; this joins the section's name-and-prayer mark to the act that leaves أثر السجود in 48:29.
terra: Calling adopted sons by their fathers preserves true lineage and belonging; it parallels the section's animal brand as a sign by which stock and owner are not confused.
terra: Faces are turned about in the Fire while their bearers wish they had obeyed God and the Messenger; rejected allegiance becomes a fiery mark on the face.
terra: ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لَهُ ٱلْمُلْكُ repeats the Lord-and-ownership formula while denying the alleged partners any possession at all.

luna: The record includes what people send ahead and وَءَاثَارَهُمْ; the section's root gloss of اثر as what remains becomes the deeds' continuing trace. | terra: وَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوا۟ وَءَاثَارَهُمْ says both deeds sent ahead and the traces they leave are written; choice therefore survives as an attributable أثر after the actor.
luna: With mouths sealed, hands speak and feet testify to what people earned; the body becomes an indelible record of the choices that marked it.
terra: The condemned found their fathers astray; it identifies the owners of the bad tracks into which they hurry in 37:70.
terra: فَهُمْ عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِمْ يُهْرَعُونَ pictures people rushing along their ancestors' traces, making a chosen allegiance recognizable as a followed trail toward punishment.
terra: وَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِم مُّصْبِحِينَ tells the audience that they pass Lot's ruins by morning, turning the vanished people into a repeatedly visible trace.
terra: Passing the ruins by night is followed by أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ, demanding inference from the scene just as the section's mutawassim reads meaning from remains.
terra: سُبْحَـٰنَ رَبِّكَ ... عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ is an explicit command-formula of keeping the Lord free of defective descriptions, the sense the section hears in purifying His mark.
terra: ذَٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لَهُ ٱلْمُلْكُ explicitly joins “your Lord” to possession of dominion, confirming the section's owner-sense of rabb.
luna: The crops grow in varied colors, yellow, then become debris; this repeated plant cycle makes the remnant after flourishing visible.
terra: Those who lied about God appear on Resurrection with faces blackened; the lie about the true Lord becomes an identifying face-mark.

luna: The former peoples left آثارًا فِي الْأَرْضِ, yet greater strength and earthly traces did not save them; the verse gives the section's trace a limit. | terra: The audience is sent through the earth to see the outcome of stronger peoples with greater ءَاثَارًا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ; trace-reading becomes moral recognition from ruins.

luna: This life is only temporary enjoyment, while the Hereafter is the abiding home; it restates the trace's passing/remaining boundary. | terra: The worldly life is only temporary enjoyment whereas the Hereafter is the enduring abode, restating the precise duration test by which the section judges preference.

luna: This repeated account again speaks of earlier peoples' آثارًا فِي الْأَرْضِ and their end; their impressive marks remain evidence of power, not permanence. | terra: The repeated command to travel and see peoples with more آثار in the earth makes surviving works into marks whose owners and fate can still be known.

luna: Hearing, sight, and skins testify to what people did; the body preserves evidence of action, turning a mark into testimony. | terra: Hearing, sight, and skins testify to what their owners did, so the hide itself discloses the life attached to it, like the section's mark that identifies its bearer.

luna: The skins answer that Allah made them speak; this completes 41:20's bodily testimony and shows that the trace cannot be concealed from its owner. | terra: The condemned ask their skins why they testified, and the skins name God as the one who made them speak; the body's surface becomes a truthful owner-linked record rather than a mute hide.

luna: One who desires the Hereafter's harvest has it increased, while one who desires this world's harvest receives only it and has no share in the Hereafter; the preference's result is made explicit.

terra: Ships at sea are likened to aʿlām, towering visible landmarks; if that noun is heard through the section's ʿ-l-m sense of a distinguishing sign, it supplies a large-scale mark recognizable at a distance.

luna: The same worldly-enjoyment versus better, lasting provision with Allah is restated for believers; it makes the section's mark of preference consequential. | terra: What people are given is enjoyment of worldly life, while what is with God is خَيْرٌۭ وَأَبْقَىٰ for believers; enduring ownership supplies the criterion of preference.
terra: The same face-darkening at the news of a daughter is repeated while the man chokes with grief, confirming the face as the outward trace of a hidden preference.
terra: The idolaters claim وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم مُّهْتَدُونَ, treating ancestral tracks as guidance; inherited preference leaves a path by which the present community is identified.
terra: وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم مُّقْتَدُونَ repeats that allegiance as following forebears' traces, showing a mark transmitted by imitation rather than received from the true Lord.
terra: Worldly embellishment is called mere enjoyment, while the Hereafter with the Lord belongs to the mindful; the owner and the enduring destination determine the better preference.

luna: A person makes desire a god, then hearing and heart are sealed and sight covered; the chosen allegiance leaves a mark on the faculties that receive signs. | terra: The person who takes desire as a god is sealed on hearing and heart; the governing preference becomes a divine mark upon the chooser's faculties.
luna: أَثَٰرَةٍ مِّنْ عِلْمٍ means a surviving remnant of knowledge demanded as evidence; this is the section's trace-as-remainder idea turned into proof of a claim.
terra: The wind destroys the people so completely that only their dwellings can be seen; ownerless structures remain as readable traces of vanished bearers and judgment.

luna: The hypocrites would be known by their marks and by the tone of their speech; hidden allegiance becomes legible through outward signs and words. | terra: فَلَعَرَفْتَهُم بِسِيمَاهُمْ says the hypocrites could be recognized by their marks and then by their speech; identity discloses itself through an outward trace.

luna: The section names أثر as a branch of the root behind تُؤْثِرُونَ; here مِنْ أَثَرِ ٱلسُّجُودِ is the visible trace left by prayer, a good mark set against the brand of disgrace. | terra: سِيمَاهُمْ فِى وُجُوهِهِم مِّنْ أَثَرِ ٱلسُّجُودِ is the section's positive face-mark exactly: worship leaves an أثر by which the Lord's companions are known.

terra: This ayah identifies the objects in 51:34 as stones of clay sent against a criminal people, so the following divine mark is an assignment of a particular instrument to particular owners of guilt.
terra: مُسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ again describes the stones assigned to the transgressors, making the divine owner's identifying mark also a designation of destination.

luna: The idols are called names invented by people without divine authority; the ayah distinguishes a label from the Lord who truly owns and judges. | terra: The idols are again called mere names coined without divine authority, exposing a name that falsely assigns sacred identity rather than revealing its true owner.
luna: The Prophet is told to turn from one who turns away from the Reminder and desires only worldly life; this joins neglected remembrance to the section's defining preference.
terra: The raised ships are again compared to aʿlām; the lexical bridge may mean mountains rather than signs here, but either reading makes them conspicuous forms that distinguish the horizon.

luna: Everything on earth perishes; the section's trace and preference theme is set against what can vanish. | terra: كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ states the disappearance side of the section's contrast between passing preference and a surviving remainder.

luna: The face of the Lord remains; this names the enduring owner behind the section's contrast between the passing world and the Lord's mark. | terra: وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ names the Lord as what remains after all earthly bearers pass, grounding permanence in the owner rather than in the temporary mark.

luna: Criminals are known بِسِيمَاهُمْ before being seized by forelocks and feet; a visible sign identifies the person for judgment, echoing the snout brand. | terra: يُعْرَفُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيمَاهُمْ makes criminals known by their marks before they are seized, realizing the section's definition of a sign that distinguishes its bearer.
terra: تَبَـٰرَكَ ٱسْمُ رَبِّكَ closes the surah by blessing the Lord's name itself, treating the name as the bearer of His majesty and honor.
terra: The question about the fire people kindle opens the immediate context of the glorify-the-name command in 56:74, placing ordinary visible fire before the Lord's name.
terra: God says He made that fire تَذْكِرَةً, a reminder or sign; it therefore already functions as something from which its maker and a greater fire are recognized before 56:74.
terra: فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ repeats the command to glorify the Lord's name immediately after the passage makes kindled fire a reminder, bringing the section's name and fire together.
terra: تَصْلِيَةُ جَحِيمٍ supplies the fire fate directly before the renewed command to glorify the Lord's name in 56:96, reproducing the image's two possible signs.
terra: After the lodging of Hellfire in 56:94, فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ again places the purified Lord-name beside the alternative fire-sign.

luna: The worldly life is pictured as rain-fed growth that yellows and becomes debris; the scene meets 87:4-5's pasture turned dark stubble and exposes the passing world. | terra: Worldly life is likened to vegetation that impresses, yellows, and becomes debris before the lasting outcomes arrive; it shows the chosen world's visible trace passing away.
terra: Messengers and Jesus are sent عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم, again using traces for a continuing relation across absent generations rather than a merely visible footprint.
terra: كَتَبَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلْإِيمَـٰنَ makes faith an inscription in the hearts of God's party, a positive inward counterpart to the fire-brand and the rust of earning.
terra: وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ reverses self-serving preference: the Helpers prefer others despite need, so the same root can leave a mark of generosity rather than attachment to الدنيا.
terra: The divine titles ٱلْقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَـٰمُ clear the named Lord of defect immediately before 59:24 joins His beautiful names to universal glorification.

luna: Allah's beautiful names belong to the Creator and Fashioner, and all creation glorifies Him; the owner-name relation gives substance to the section's expanded reading of tasbih. | terra: لَهُ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ is joined in the same ayah to all creation glorifying Him, directly uniting the Lord's names with tasbih.
luna: Believers are warned not to let wealth and children distract them from remembrance of Allah; doing so marks the losing side of the section's choice.
terra: The command not to obey every habitual swearer and contemptible man begins the portrait whose traits culminate in the brand of 68:16; the addressee must read character before following it.
terra: هَمَّازٍۢ مَّشَّآءٍۭ بِنَمِيمٍ supplies the slander and tale-bearing traits of the bearer branded in 68:16, making the punishment an identifying summary of lived character.
terra: The branded man's portrait continues with hindering good, aggression, and sin; these are further lived traits that the bodily mark of 68:16 makes publicly identifiable.

terra: The portrait adds harshness and the disputed epithet zanīm immediately before the motive and response that lead to branding; this ayah contributes the bearer's already distinguishing moral identity.
terra: His possession of wealth and sons supplies the worldly status surrounding his rejection of the verses; the eventual brand overturns the identity he drew from those possessions.
terra: أَسَـٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ is what the soon-to-be-branded man calls the revelations; it makes his treatment of the “first” records the identifying act answered by 68:16.

luna: The section's disputed reading of ٱسْمَ in 87:1 through the dictionary root و س م becomes literal in سَنَسِمُهُۥ عَلَى ٱلْخُرْطُومِ: the rejecter of recited signs receives an identifying stigma on his nose. | terra: The threat سَنَسِمُهُۥ عَلَى ٱلْخُرْطُومِ is the Qur'an's literal act of branding a person; it turns the section's identifying livestock mark into the visible judgment of a character.

terra: After the destroyed people, the question asks whether any remnant of them can be seen; total erasure supplies the boundary case for the section's أثر as what remains visible after its owner is gone.
terra: فَسَبِّحْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلْعَظِيمِ is the same stance and nearly the same command as the section's opening; the name is something actively kept in glorification.
terra: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا joins remembering the Lord's name to exclusive devotion, making the named owner distinguish the servant's allegiance.
luna: The source section names ء ث ر through تُؤْثِرُونَ; سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ here uses that root in the different sense of transmitted magic, the rejecter's dismissal that leads into Saqar at 74:26.
luna: The claim that the rejecter will be cast into Saqar connects the dismissal in 74:24 with a bodily fire mark in 74:29, echoing the section's pairing of rejection and fire.
luna: Saqar leaves nothing and spares nothing; beside the section's trace-as-remainder, this is a specific reversal where destructive fire erases rather than leaves a mark.

luna: Saqar is described as scorching human skin; the fire leaves a bodily stigma, a negative counterpart to the devotional trace on faces. | terra: لَوَّاحَةٌ لِّلْبَشَرِ describes Hell as scorching or altering the skin; it is the fire-mark on hide made into eschatological judgment.

luna: بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ states love of the immediate life, the same preference identified in 87:16. | terra: بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ restates the attraction to the immediate life as the controlling love by which the audience is identified.

luna: وَتَذَرُونَ الْآخِرَةَ supplies the other half of 75:20's choice; it completes the section's contrast with the life that remains. | terra: وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ gives the other side of that preference: choosing the immediate necessarily leaves the lasting life behind.
terra: Radiant faces on the Day begin a direct facial distinction between good and evil outcomes, the eschatological form of reading a person's trace in the face.
terra: Those radiant faces look toward their Lord, identifying the allegiance and hope expressed by their visible condition.
terra: Other faces are gloomy, furnishing the contrary visible mark on the bearers of a feared outcome.
terra: The gloomy faces expect a crushing calamity, explaining the judgment their appearance already discloses.
terra: وَٱذْكُرِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ commands regular remembrance of the Lord's name, the positive sign of allegiance opposed to being known by fire.

luna: They love the immediate life and leave a heavy day behind; the verse makes the preference's neglected aftermath explicit. | terra: إِنَّ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ يُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ identifies a people by love of the immediate and neglect of a heavy coming day, matching the section's claim that preference marks the chooser.
terra: Transgression identifies the person whose preference is stated in 79:38; it contributes the moral character that the following choice and fire outcome disclose.

luna: وَءَاثَرَ الْحَيَوٰةَ الدُّنْيَا uses the same root as the section's تَؤْثِرُونَ for preferring worldly life; this is its most direct parallel for a choice that leaves a recognizable trace. | terra: وَءَاثَرَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا repeats the section's preference almost word for word, making the chosen world the decisive identifier of the transgressor.

luna: The refuge of the one who preferred worldly life is Hell; the neighboring verse makes the section's pairing of choice and fire explicit. | terra: فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ states the fire outcome of 79:38's worldly preference, completing the same preference-to-fire movement as this image.

luna: The one who fears standing before the Lord and restrains desire is the reversal of the one who prefers the world, matching the section's two marks. | terra: The person who fears standing before his Lord and restrains desire is the opposing character to the one who preferred worldly life in 79:38.

luna: The refuge for that restrained person is the Garden, completing the boundary opposite the Hell in 79:39. | terra: Paradise becomes the home of that restrained person, completing the alternative to the fire-home attached to worldly preference.
terra: Faces on that Day are bright, beginning a paired portrait in which inward outcome is readable on the face.
terra: Other faces have dust upon them, giving the contrary group a visible residue or mark.
terra: The bearers of the darkened faces are identified as disbelieving transgressors, completing the inference from facial sign to moral identity.

luna: The section says what one prefers leaves a trace; here earnings have laid rust over the heart, an inner imprint of a person's acts. | terra: رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ makes earned conduct a coating on the heart, a precise inner version of the section's claim that preference leaves its mark on the person.
terra: تَعْرِفُ فِى وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ ٱلنَّعِيمِ makes bliss recognizable in faces, supplying the good face-trace paired with the section's good-or-evil reading.
luna: The righteous are given a sealed drink, the object whose khitām is described in 83:26; if khitām means a seal, this offers a good mark opposite the stigma of the brand.

luna: خِتَامُهُ مِسْكٌ may mean the drink's seal or its finishing taste; on the seal reading, musk identifies the righteous drink and reverses the fire brand, while the taste reading is a weaker parallel.
terra: Faces are humbled on the overwhelming Day, making abasement bodily visible before their labor and fire destination are stated.
terra: Those humbled faces enter a scorching fire, joining the readable facial condition to the section's alternative fire-sign.
terra: Other faces are joyful, supplying the positive facial mark opposite the humbled, fire-bound group.

luna: The Hereafter is better than the first life; this is the section's contrast between the preferred near life and what endures. | terra: The later life is declared better for the Prophet than the first, a concise reversal of preferring the nearer or earlier portion merely because it is present.
terra: ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ makes the Lord's name the sign under which recitation begins, expressing action conducted in the owner's allegiance.
terra: The rejecter is threatened with seizure by the forelock, placing judgment on a conspicuous part of the head as the brand in 68:16 is placed on the snout.
terra: The forelock is itself called lying and sinful, attaching moral identity to a body part in the same way a brand makes the bearer's character legible.
luna: On the quake day the earth reports its news; the ground itself retains and reveals traces of what happened on it.
luna: The next ayah says the earth reports because its Lord inspired it, completing 99:4's image of the ground as a witness to its traces.
terra: The one who gathers and counts wealth supplies the worldly attachment whose eventual fire reaches inward in 104:6-7.
terra: نَارُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُوقَدَةُ is the divine fire awaiting the wealth-counter, connecting a preferred possession to the Lord's contrary mark.
terra: The fire تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى ٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةِ, reaching the hearts; the outward brand becomes an inward disclosure of what the person loved.
